SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349 PUC DOCKET NO. 59475 

JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICE CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJEСТ

MOTION TO ENTER DIRECT TESTIMONY to EXHIBITS already submitted 

COMES NOW Dr. Jennifer S. Reppond, Party No. 91 as identified in Attachment A & B, and MSG. Travis W. Reppond to the Procedural Order, appearing Pro Se, and respectfully file this Motion to Enter Direct Testimony and Exhibits, and in support thereof would show the following: 

1. On May 12, 2026, Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond timely filed their Direct Testimony with the Public Utility Commission of Texas. Docket filing number 3919. 
2. On June 2, 2026, all exhibits supporting the testimony previously filed in this proceeding were uploaded to the PUCT Interchange under Filing No. 5469, as well as to the Kiteworks and Egnyte repositories, together with the corresponding Exhibit List. At that time, it was not clear that the original testimony, which these exhibits were intended to support, also needed to be uploaded as part of that submission.
During the prehearing conference on June 5, 2026, we became aware that the testimony itself had not been included with the June 2 filing. After reviewing SOAH 30, Attachment A, I noted that my testimony was not listed and that Exhibit Set 2 also appeared to be missing. I raised this issue with the Administrative Law Judge during the prehearing conference.
The Administrative Law Judge instructed me to refile the testimony through the PUCT Interchange [5851] and to upload the testimony to the Kiteworks and Egnyte repositories. Upon receiving that instruction, I promptly complied and uploaded the testimony to all required locations.
The omission was unintentional and resulted from a misunderstanding regarding the filing requirements. Upon learning of the issue, corrective action was taken immediately to ensure that the testimony and supporting materials were properly submitted and available for consideration.
3. Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond respectfully request that the attached testimony and exhibit be accepted into the record and considered by the State Office of Administrative Hearings and all parties in this proceeding. 
4. Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond are appearing Pro Se in this matter. 
5. Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond do not intend to call any witnesses other than themselves. 
6. Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond do not request cross-examination. 
7. The attached Direct Testimony is offered as an exhibit in this proceeding (refiled for a third time) to accompany the previously filed Exhibit List and Exhibit Sets 1 and 2.
WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Dr. Jennifer Reppond and MSG Travis Reppond respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges accept this Direct Testimony into the record, together with the Exhibit List and all supporting exhibits previously submitted, including Exhibit Sets 1 and 2. Dr. Reppond and MSG Reppond further request confirmation that all testimony and supporting exhibits are included in the evidentiary record and grant such other and further relief to which they may be justly entitled.

PERSONAL INFORMATION:
Q. Please state your name and address.
A. My name is Dr. Jennifer S. Reppond and my husband, Master Sergeant Travis W. Reppond (Ret.), and I are the owners and residents of a 20.5-acre property located at 10048 Wallace Road, Holland, Texas (Parcel ID 3049).
Q. Are you the same Dr. Jennifer S. Reppond and Master Sergeant Travis W. Reppond (Ret.) who filed a Motion to Intervene in this proceeding?
A. Yes. PUC Docket Number 59475, filed on 3-31-2026, Item Number 144, Motion to Intervene. We are in opposition to Link D11.
Q. Are you testifying on behalf of the above-listed landowner?
A. Yes.
Q. Is the property affected by the transmission line project proposed by Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC?
A. Yes.
Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?
A. The purpose of this testimony is to provide factual information regarding the anticipated impact of the proposed 765kV transmission line and associated structures, as contemplated under Route D-11, on our property, its use, its value, and the conditions under which it functions as both a residence and a working property.
This testimony is not an objection to the project as a whole, but to the specific routing that would impose a disproportionate and cumulative impact on this property
Q. What are the routes on this property?
A.  Route Link D11
Q. What routes do you oppose?
A. Route Link D11
Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?
A. No.
DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION
Q. Is there an occupied residence on the property?
A. Yes. The property contains an occupied residential structure that serves as our primary residence.
Q. Is the residence reflected on publicly available mapping imagery and county GIS records?
A. Yes. The residence is visible on publicly available GIS and aerial mapping imagery associated with property.
Q. Description of the property?
A. The property consists of approximately 20.5 acres and serves as our primary residence. The land extends approximately 1,800 feet from the front fence line to the back fence line, with our residence located approximately 700 feet from the front boundary. The property is actively used for multiple purposes beyond residential occupancy. We grow vegetables on the property and maintain livestock operations, including cattle, chickens, and pigs. The property also includes a pond supported by an artesian water source. The property supports local wildlife and is used for hunting, reflecting the presence of an established habitat consistent with the current rural and agricultural character of the land.
Q. Are there additional improvements associated with the residence?
A. Yes. In addition to the residence itself, the property includes fencing, cross-fencing, agricultural structures, and additional residential improvements and agricultural improvements that support the current use and functionality of the property.
Q. Why is this important to your testimony?
A. The proximity of the proposed 765kV transmission infrastructure must be evaluated in relation to the existence of an occupied residential structure and the surrounding improvements associated with the current residential and agricultural use of the property.
Q. What is the proximity of existing and proposed transmission infrastructure to your residence?
A. The property is currently affected by existing high-voltage transmission infrastructure located approximately 1,000 feet from the residence. Under the proposed Route D-11 alignment, substantially larger 765kV transmission structures would be introduced at a closer distance, approximately 500 feet from the residence.
Q. What are the size and physical characteristics of the proposed transmission structures? 
A. The proposed transmission structures are expected to reach approximately 300 feet in height and represent significantly larger infrastructure than what currently exists near the property.
Q. What easement and clearance requirements will affect your property?
A. The proposed project requires an easement corridor of approximately 200 feet in width. In addition, an existing transmission structure is located near the rear of the property, and any new structure must maintain required clearance distances from that infrastructure. These requirements create overlapping zones of restriction across the property.
Q. Does the proposed route represent expansion or consolidation of infrastructure?
A. The proposed routing represents an expansion of transmission infrastructure across the property rather than consolidation within an existing corridor.



LAND USE, CONCERNS AND HISTORY
Q. How will the easement affect your property use?
A. The proposed easement would impose substantial restrictions on the use of land within the corridor, including limitations on structures, vegetation, and improvements. These restrictions would reduce usable land, limit flexibility, and interfere with both current and future use.
Q. Will the project fragment or divide your property?
A. Yes. The placement of the transmission corridor would divide the property into separate sections, interfering with movement, land management, and overall functionality.
Q. Will this affect future development or use of your property?
A. Yes. The easement and clearance requirements would reduce buildable area and limit future improvements and expansion
Q. How will the project affect agricultural use?
A. The property is actively used for vegetable cultivation and livestock management. The transmission easement would limit access and interfere with these activities. Livestock may be affected by electrical conditions such as stray voltage and ground current, and may exhibit behavioral changes including avoidance and stress responses.


Q. How will the project affect soil and land conditions?
A. Construction and maintenance activities involving heavy equipment may cause soil compaction and drainage changes, which can negatively affect agricultural productivity.
Q. How will the project affect water resources on your property?
A. The property includes a pond supported by an artesian water source. This feature depends on stable environmental and subsurface conditions. Construction and land disturbance may affect access, maintenance, and sustainability of this feature.
Q. Will vegetation management affect your property?
A. Yes. Transmission easements require vegetation clearing and growth restrictions, which would alter the natural landscape and interfere with current land management practices.
Q. How will the project affect wildlife and hunting?
A. The property supports wildlife and is used for hunting. Changes associated with construction, vegetation clearing, and large infrastructure may alter wildlife movement patterns and habitat conditions.
FINANCIAL RISKS
Q. What financial risks does this project pose?
A. The property represents a significant financial asset. The project would reduce usable land and impose restrictions that affect value and financial stability.
Q. How may the project affect property value and marketability?
A. Properties near high-voltage transmission lines may experience reduced buyer interest, particularly when structures are large and visible. Reduced buyer interest may result in longer time on the market and fewer potential buyers making the property less valuable.
HEALTH RISKS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND WILDLIFE
Q. What concerns do you have regarding noise?
A. High-voltage transmission lines produce audible noise under certain environmental conditions, which would introduce a continuous environmental factor not currently present.
Q. What concerns do you have regarding autism and sensory sensitivity?
A. My son is autistic and has sensory processing needs. Research indicates heightened sensitivity to sound. The introduction of persistent environmental noise may affect his ability to function comfortably.
Q. What concerns do you have regarding traumatic brain injury?
A. My husband is a combat-wounded veteran who sustained a  traumatic brain injury (TBI) during military service which is associated with sensitivity to noise and difficulty processing sound.


Q. What concerns do you have regarding medical devices?
A. As a result of combat-related injuries, my husband relies on implanted spinal cord stimulators. Research has examined electromagnetic interaction with such devices, and proximity to a 765kV transmission line creates a reasonable concern.
Q. What concerns do you have regarding electromagnetic fields?
A. While no definitive causal relationship has been established, electromagnetic fields have been classified as possibly carcinogenic in research. Some studies report associations with certain health outcomes, while others do not.
Q. What do you think will be the risks to your agricultural activities and animals?
A. Our property is used for agricultural and rural residential purposes, including the care of animals. Research regarding high-voltage transmission lines and their effects on livestock and wildlife is mixed, but some studies have reported concerns related to animal stress, behavior, and environmental disruption from factors such as audible noise and electromagnetic exposure. In addition, the presence of a 765kV transmission corridor could disrupt the natural use of our land, affect wildlife movement, and alter the quiet rural environment that currently supports our animals and agricultural activities.
RECREATION, COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS
Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?
A. Our family chose this property for its quiet rural setting, privacy, and peaceful environment. The presence of a 765kV transmission line would significantly change the character of the property through its visual impact, continual industrial presence, and associated noise, affecting our ability to fully enjoy and use our land as we currently do.
Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use on your land?
A.  Yes. The proposed transmission line could limit future use and development of the property by restricting how portions of the land may be used and by reducing the flexibility we currently have for agriculture, residential, and recreational purposes.
Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your area?
A. Our community values the quiet, open, and rural nature of the area. The introduction of a large 765kV transmission line would change the character of the community by introducing a major industrial structure into a primarily rural and residential environment.
Q. How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?
A. The size and visibility of a 765kV transmission line and its structures would substantially alter the natural appearance of our property and surrounding landscape. One of the main reasons we chose this property was its natural beauty, including the large tree line and pond that help sustain the landscape and privacy of the property. This visual impact would negatively affect the scenic and rural character that drew us to this property.

Q. Do transmission routes parallel any existing rights of way on your property?
A. No existing right of way on our property is comparable in scale or impact to a proposed 765kV transmission corridor.
Q. Does Oncor’s application properly identify the structures on your property?
A. To the best of our knowledge, we have concerns that the application may not fully or accurately reflect all structures, improvements, and the overall use of our property. 
ADDITIONAL PROPERTY IMPACTS
Q. Will the utility have access to your property?
A. Yes. Transmission easements typically allow ongoing access for inspection, maintenance, and repair, resulting in periodic entry by personnel and equipment
Q. Will the utility have access to your property?
A. Yes. Transmission easements typically allow ongoing access for inspection, maintenance, and repair, resulting in periodic entry by personnel and equipment.
Q. Will fencing or land management be affected?
A. Yes. Adjustments to fencing and livestock management practices may be required.
Q. Are the impacts temporary or permanent?
A. The impacts are permanent. Transmission infrastructure of this scale represents long-term change.

Q. Will this affect future generations?
A. Yes. The property is intended to remain within our family, and any reduction in value or usability will affect future ownership
CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION
Q. What is your overall conclusion?
A. The proposed transmission line would have a materially negative impact on this property due to combined physical, functional, economic, environmental, and health-related factors.
Q. Does this conclude your testimony?
A. Yes.
